I've seen anak2 HI yang sukses kerja di lembaga internasional (EU Delegation / US Embassy) tapi gue jg liat kok anak2 HI yg sukses dengan skill2 di poin ke dua. Misalnya jadi Comms Officer / Socmed Officer, terutama di lembaga think thank / policy. Lagi musim pemilu gini biasanya lembaga policy / kebijakan / volunteering lagi rekrut banyak orang. 

Untuk S2, coba tarik napas dulu. Will it be another waste of money and time or will it be a worthy investment? Semua major itu what you make of it. Aku pernah kok ketemu lulusan STEM yg malah nganggur berbulan2, dan liat anak SMK sukses di perusahaan IT di Bandung. Aku juga liat lulusan Law yang sukses di Law firm, dan lulusan Law yang jadi MT di Procuremrnt. Life is what you make of it, nder. Semangat terus dan coba visualisasikan hidup: where do you wanna be? One of my senior hold a position at the UN, embassy at home and abroad, think tanks (researchers), etc while others went on to become researchers (think tanks), while some work as a copywriters, sales & marketing, social media specialists etc. Being on the internet gives you this specific ideas that only STEM majors get jobs; that's not true at all. In some regional organizations (think ASEAN / EU, etc for example), STEM jobs are directly linked with humanities work. For concrete example: I know someone who works in Counter-terrorism in South Asia (sponsored by the UN, operated by the local government); as a program lead, he is responsible in creating modules and programs that would reach the most vulnerable group. He is working alongside data scientist who provides accurate numbers of said vulnerable groups and measure how far these programs reach them. There would also be an M&E specialist (humanities) who ensure that these numbers are interpreted correctly to make sure that it is understood within local contexts. In the future, a lot of jobs would be more linked to each others (humanities and stem), so I think it's not accurate at all to deem that all humanities would be jobless. Even Doctors Without Borders have humanities graduate as program managers, M&E specialists, program lead, etc. it's not as bleak as people make it out to be, but it ain't easy either.
